final_answer:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - INTERNAL
TO: Marcus Yuen; Diane Holbrook. CC: Sarah Lindgren. FROM: David Koh. RE: Buy-Side CIM Analysis, Cascade Environmental Solutions, Inc. (CES), Fund III. Basis: matter timeline (IOI due 7/14/2025); Thornfield sector memo (6/12/2025) used as benchmark framework only, not independently verified. Legal currentness checked 10/2/2026.

1. BOTTOM LINE
CES is a credible platform, but the CIM overstates value. (a) Its own bridge does not foot: $12.1M plus $4.7M of adjustments is $16.8M, not $17.1M. (b) Every add-back is contestable; a diligence-adjusted FY2024 Adjusted EBITDA of roughly $14.8M-$16.1M (illustrative, my assumptions below) implies EV of about $118M-$161M at 8.0x-10.0x versus the CIM's $136.8M-$171.0M. (c) The largest customer (PNR, 21.4%) shows a contract that expired 3/31/2025. (d) The CIM and Greenleaf's own exhibits and customer report contradict each other on financials and customers. (e) Maintenance capex, DSO and the PFAS plan look flattering. Recommendation: submit an IOI only on conditions (Section 8), price off a buyer-adjusted EBITDA, and do not accept the 17.1 headline. Also, the Thornfield memo says CES "fits squarely" in Fund III's $30M-$100M EV band; even our adjusted range exceeds it. Confirm LPA concentration limits and IC approval before submitting.

2. ADJUSTED EBITDA (CIM VI.C; Exhibits "EBITDA Bridge"; App. B)
- Arithmetic: 1.9+0.8+1.2+0.4+0.3+0.1 = 4.7; 12.1+4.7 = 16.8. Overstatement $0.3M (about $2.4M-$3.0M EV at 8-10x); true margin 19.2%, not 19.6%; FY21-24 Adjusted EBITDA CAGR about 20.1%, not 20.8%. FY2021-23 columns foot; only FY2024 fails.
- Owner compensation ($1.9M): implied replacement CEO cost in the CIM's own App. B falls from $0.7M (FY21, FY22) to $0.6M (FY23) to $0.5M (FY24) (exhibit comp $2.1M-$2.4M less add-back), so the assumption is a moving target. $0.5M for a CEO running a $90M, four-state, PFAS-growth business with the founder exiting in 18-24 months is low. Illustrative: $0.8M replacement cuts the add-back to $1.6M. Verify the $2.4M composition, since it includes "personal expenses". Projections (Exhibits, Income Statement) drop owner compensation to zero in FY2025E-27E with no CEO cost, overstating projected profit by at least $0.5M a year.
- Related-party lease ($0.8M): rent $1.4M to Oakes (2019-2029, 8.5 acres). The "market" $0.6M is a management estimate; CIM IV.C itself cites $1.0M-$1.2M for comparable specialized staging facilities, which cuts the add-back to $0.2M-$0.4M. The lease runs to 2029, so the add-back is not realized unless Oakes amends it at closing; absent that, treat as zero. Process letter item 2 invites our proposal on this property.
- DEQ matter ($1.2M): $875K settlement plus $325K fees (8/14/2024), for improper storage of contaminated soils at the Portland yard, the operating core. FY2023 also carries a $0.2M "legal/regulatory" add-back, so this is not isolated. Thornfield benchmark: $200K-$500K recurring annual run-rate; defensible add-back about $0.7M-$1.0M (Thornfield memo 5.2; two-company sample, so persuasive, not conclusive). Exhibits book the $875K in "Other Income/(Expense)," below EBIT; if reported EBITDA never deducted it, the add-back double counts. Consent agreement terms (corrective action, stipulated penalties, license conditions) are undisclosed.
- Other: "non-recurring" costs recur ($0.1M, $0.2M, $0.4M in FY22-24; relabelled from "equipment relocation"), and the CIM describes the Boise depot as established 2018 and "expanded," not relocated; the $0.4M may be capex. Phantom units ($0.3M) recur annually; cash settlement at closing is a debt-like seller cost and removes retention incentives. IT $0.1M: accept subject to invoices.
- Illustrative ranges: Low = 12.1 + 1.4 owner + 0 lease + 0.7 regulatory + 0.2 relocation + 0.3 phantom + 0.1 IT = $14.8M. High = 12.1 + 1.9 + 0.4 + 0.9 + 0.4 + 0.3 + 0.1 = $16.1M. Forward EV ($157.6M-$197.0M on $19.7M) inherits all errors.

3. PFAS GROWTH THESIS
- PFAS: $1.1M, $3.4M, $6.2M; plan $14.0M, $22.0M, $27.0M (+125.8%, +57.1%). It is 64% of FY24-26 growth ($15.8M of $24.7M). Exhibits imply traditional remediation grows only 1.2% in FY2025E ($42.0M to $42.5M), so the plan is a PFAS bet.
- Thornfield expects 30%-50% company growth, so about $8.1M-$9.3M in FY2025 and $10.5M-$14.0M in FY2026: a $4.7M-$5.9M FY2025 and $8M-$11.5M FY2026 revenue gap before margin loss. Treat as persuasive: the GreenWorks analogy is a different service line (vapor intrusion).
- The CIM gives no PFAS backlog; the backlog report says only "several" PFAS contracts. Capex is inconsistent: PFAS equipment capex was $0.2M, $0.7M, $1.2M (cumulative $2.1M) for $6.2M of revenue, yet FY2025E is $0.3M for +$7.8M revenue.
- Regulatory tailwind is slower than the CIM implies. The April 2024 rule set six MCLs, with PFOA/PFOS compliance by 2029. EPA (5/2025 announcement; proposals published 5/20/2026, not final) would keep PFOA/PFOS at 4 ppt, push compliance to 2031, and rescind the other four standards. These are proposals; the CIM's "enforceable MCLs for six PFAS" is stale. Offsetting: EPA retained PFOA/PFOS CERCLA hazardous-substance designation and the D.C. Circuit denied challenges (8/18/2026), which supports site-cleanup demand. Water-utility MCL work is also not CES's core customer base.
- CIM IX.A says PFAS becomes the "largest service line" by FY2027; its own table shows $27.0M versus $35.0M (Industrial Cleaning).

4. CUSTOMERS, CONTRACTS, BACKLOG
- PNR ($18.7M; 21.4%; IC and Remediation): MSA expired 3/31/2025, before the CIM; no renewal disclosed, and the CIM's "significant majority under multi-year MSAs" is unsupported. MSAs carry no minimum volumes (Backlog Report 7.1). Illustrative loss: about $6.2M gross profit at the 33% gross margin. Require executed renewal, pricing, term and change-of-control terms before IOI/price lock; consider PNR as a condition or escrow/earnout. Do not contact PNR directly (process letter IV).
- Contract status of the top 5 ($45.8M, 52.5%): PNR expired; ODOT annual (July); Willamette Steel month-to-month; Meridian expires 12/31/2025, inside the Q4 closing window. About $38.5M (44.1% of revenue) is expired, annual, month-to-month or expiring by closing. Only Columbia Basin (to 12/31/2027) is term-secured.
- Report versus CIM conflicts: customers #6-10 are different names with identical revenue ($3.8M, $3.6M, $3.2M, $2.9M, $2.7M) and different contract types and dates (CIM: Cascade Terminals, Puget Sound Utilities, City of Portland BES, Northern Pacific Rail, Tidewater; Report: Clearwater MUD, Northshore Industrial Park, Summit Materials, Timberline, Harborview). Start dates differ (PNR 2011 v. 2012; ODOT 2013 v. 2014; Columbia Basin 2017 v. 2016; Meridian 2014 v. 2017). Report says "five or more years" and CIM "10 or more." Government revenue is 5% in the Report's contract mix but ODOT alone is 10.4%, and the sector table shows 19.2%. Geography: CIM says 75% Oregon/Washington; Report says 82.3%. The Report cites Sacramento satellite operations absent from the CIM's three-facility list.
- Backlog $42.6M ("reasonably estimable" scope, including MSAs without minimums and the expired PNR MSA). The Report says 77.5% ($33.0M) converts in FY2025, but the CIM says "12-24 months," and remediation backlog ($26.8M) is called multi-year. H1 2025 ($18.2M) should now be actual: request it. $74.0M "visibility" adds unweighted pipeline; at the stated 35%-40% win rate, pipeline yields $11.0M-$12.6M, so risk-weighted visibility is $53.6M-$55.2M. Backlog covers 33.5% of FY2025E revenue.

5. FINANCIAL INTEGRITY
- Two financial sets do not reconcile (both Greenleaf): FY2024 net income $5.0M (CIM) versus $6.7M; gross profit $29.5M versus $28.8M; cash $2.3M versus $4.1M; total assets $46.1M versus $50.0M; equity $17.1M versus $18.8M; CFO $9.2M versus $10.0M; FCF $2.0M versus $2.8M. Exhibits' EBIT plus D&A ($15.3M) does not equal reported EBITDA ($12.1M). Segment history differs (FY21 Industrial Cleaning $20.1M v. $19.2M). Retained earnings do not roll with net income and distributions. Debt: CIM $17.3M; exhibits show a term loan of $14.2M plus a separate $1.8M current portion plus $3.1M revolver ($19.1M) or a double count. Cash-free/debt-free price turns on this. Demand audited statements (Ridgeline), tax returns and trial balances.
- DSO: CIM says 52 days ("industry-leading"). AR $16.9M / $87.3M x 365 = 70.7 days (about 82 including $2.7M unbilled revenue); FY21-23 was 68-71. Thornfield's range is 45-55 days; above 60 signals collection or dispute risk. Gap about $4.5M of AR; test aging, disputes, unbilled and PNR receivables.
- Maintenance capex: $3.0M (3.4%) against 5%-7% ($4.4M-$6.1M). CIM says flat at $3.0M FY22-24, but exhibits show $2.6M, $2.8M, $3.0M, and FY2025E stays $3.0M while revenue grows 12.8%, falling to 2.7% in FY2027E. D&A ($4.2M-$4.3M) exceeds it. Counterpoint: fleet is young (4.5 years, $22M replacement value). Shortfall $1.4M-$3.1M a year; $2.5M at midpoint. Commission fleet assessment; treat deferred catch-up as debt-like. FCF has been flat near $2M-$2.8M while Adjusted EBITDA rose 76%.
- NWC: $11.8M (13.5%) is in the 10%-14% range but includes the disputed-looking AR (see DSO); set the peg on audited monthly averages.

6. REGULATORY, PEOPLE, STRUCTURE
- Licensing and capacity: only two PEs after January 2025 retirement (disclosed as a strength in the CIM, II.D item 6), yet PE sign-off is required for assessments, work plans and closure reports (CIM III.A). PFAS growth needs 2-3 more hires over 6-12 months (Thornfield). Diligence: PE licensure by state, hiring plan, and any practice-without-PE exposure.
- Key persons: Oakes (68%, 61, exiting in 18-24 months) and Prewitt (client relationships; bio says she joined in 2007 as a founding employee "prior to incorporation" though CES was formed in 2009). No retention agreements; phantom units cash out at close. Require retention, non-compete/non-solicit and a consulting agreement; GreenWorks lost a key manager within six months of closing.
- Environmental: DEQ violation was at the Portland yard owned by Oakes. Obtain Phase I/II before any purchase of the property or renewed lease; allocate pre-closing contamination to sellers. Stock deal keeps permits (Appendix D: four transporter permits, DEQ license) but also all historic liabilities: seek special indemnity, escrow, R&W insurance (environmental exclusions likely) and pollution legal liability cover. Verify permit change-of-control notices, EMR 0.87, and ISNetworld/Avetta status.
- Structure/process: stock purchase gives no basis step-up for a C-corporation (338(h)(10) unavailable) so price should reflect it. Term loan matures 8/31/2026 (repay at close). CIM says the NDA is with Greenleaf; the letter says CES: confirm counterparty and joinders. No contact with management, customers or lenders. Thornfield's memo is internal and must not be shared.

7. COVERAGE NOTE (inconsistencies also noted): process letter says CIM dated 6/9/2025; the CIM says June 2025 only; Thornfield memo's text and table use different adjusted-margin benchmarks (18-20% v. 15-18%).

8. NEXT STEPS
IOI: bid on buyer-adjusted EBITDA ($14.8M-$16.1M) with a stated range, cash-free/debt-free, debt-like items (phantom payout, deferred capex, DEQ obligations, excess AR), HQ lease amended to market with an option or ROFO to buy, PNR renewal, retention packages, and QoE, fleet, environmental, PE and customer-call diligence. First data-room requests: audited FS and reconciliation of the CIM and exhibits; QoE support for each add-back; PNR MSA and correspondence; PFAS backlog by signed contract; 10-year enforcement history and consent agreement; aged AR; fleet register; PE licences; Calloway, Barrett & Sims to review the lease, MSAs, permits and the SPA draft. Deliver by 6/25/2025.
